import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 16

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/16](https://www.erdosproblems.com/16)
- [Ch23] Chen, Yong-Gao, A conjecture of Erdős on $p+2^k$. arXiv:2312.04120 (2023).
- [Er50] Erdős, P., On integers of the form $2^k+p$ and some related problems. Summa Brasil. Math.
  (1950), 113-123.
- [Ro34] Romanoff, N. P., Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie. Math. Ann. (1934), 668-678.
-/

open Nat Filter Set
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos16

/--
The set of odd integers not of the form $2^k+p$.
-/
def Erdos16Set : Set ℕ :=
  { n | Odd n ∧ ¬ ∃ k p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n = 2 ^ k + p }

/--
A set of natural numbers has density 0.
-/
def density_zero (S : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦ (count (· ∈ S) x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0)

/--
Is the set of odd integers not of the form $2^k+p$ the union of an infinite arithmetic progression
and a set of density $0$?

Erdős called this conjecture "rather silly".

Chen [Ch23] has proved the answer is no.

This was formalized in Lean by Chin using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/danielchin/proofs/blob/main/Proofs/ErdosProblems/Erdos16.lean"]
theorem erdos_16 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∃ A B : Set ℕ, Erdos16Set = A ∪ B ∧
        (∃ a d : ℕ, d > 0 ∧ A = { x | ∃ m : ℕ, x = a + m * d }) ∧
        density_zero B := by
  sorry

/--
A set of natural numbers has positive lower density.
-/
def positive_lower_density (S : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  0 < atTop.liminf (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((count (· ∈ S) n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) : EReal))

/--
Romanoff [Ro34] showed that the set of odd integers of this form has positive density.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_16.variant.romanoff :
    let S := { n : ℕ | Odd n ∧ ∃ k p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n = 2 ^ k + p }
    positive_lower_density S := by
  sorry

/--
Using covering congruences Erdős [Er50] proved that the set of odd integers which are not of this
form contains an infinite arithmetic progression.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_16.variant.erdos :
    ∃ a d : ℕ, d > 0 ∧ { x | ∃ m : ℕ, x = a + m * d } ⊆ Erdos16Set := by
  sorry

end Erdos16

reformulations.difference: Lean permits k=0, whereas Chen explicitly takes k to be a positive integer and lists 3 among the unrepresentable integers. Consequently, Chen's set is `insert 3 Erdos16Set`, not literally `Erdos16Set`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For odd n, a representation with k=0 requires n=1+p with p=2, hence n=3. This singleton difference changes none of the three theorem statements: positive lower density is invariant under finite changes; an infinite arithmetic progression survives removal of finitely many points by taking a tail; and an AP-plus-density-zero decomposition survives finite changes by taking an AP tail and absorbing the remaining finite exceptions into the density-zero set. The singleton identity and the equivalences for all three statements were proved in /workspace/review/complete_check.lean without sorry dependencies.

reformulations.difference: The formal statement uses positive lower density rather than asserting existence of a positive natural-density limit, although the prose says 'positive density'.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Romanoff's footnote 1 on p.668 defines positive density by an eventual positive lower bound N(x)/x > α. Erdős's 1950 introduction likewise explains the result as a counting function greater than c₁x. This is precisely positive lower density, not existence of a density limit. In scratch Lean, `positive_lower_density S` was proved equivalent to `∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c ≤ count (· ∈ S) n / n`, with real-valued ratios. Strict versus non-strict lower bounds are equivalent after shrinking c. The EReal formulation introduces no exceptional behavior: the ratios lie in [0,1], and EReal division agrees with embedded real division.

sources_consulted: Yong-Gao Chen, A conjecture of Erdős on p+2^k, arXiv:2312.04120v3, §1, especially Conjecture A, Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, and the introductory discussion of Romanoff and Erdős: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2312.04120 ; version history: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04120 .
P. Erdős, On integers of the form 2^k+p and some related problems (1950), introduction and Theorem 3 on p.113, proof and remarks on pp.119–120: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1950-07.pdf .

N. P. Romanoff, Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie (1934), p.668, Satz II and footnote 1, read from the Göttingen scan: https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/pdf/PPN235181684_0109/LOG_0046.pdf .

review.notes: All three definitions and three theorem statements were checked, including quantifiers, conjunctions, answer polarity, arithmetic-progression infinitude, and empty/zero/small inputs. No mathematical defects or stale statuses were found. The cited proof defines its `density_zero` predicate as containing no infinite AP. That predicate is weaker than genuine density zero, so its nonexistence theorem is stronger and suffices. I compiled the linked proof and formally bridged it to an exact copy of the repository's main theorem, also deriving the Erdős variant. The resulting declarations in /workspace/review/complete_check.lean use only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The erdosproblems.com page returned a Cloudflare challenge despite a descriptive User-Agent; the cited primary papers and checked formal proof independently settled the statements and statuses. Detailed checklist notes are in /workspace/review/review_notes.md.
